name: AI Data-Centre Liquid Cooling: Fluids, Hoses & Heat Exchangers
scope: Indian listed suppliers of coolants/dielectric fluids, liquid-cooling skids and hoses, and heat exchangers/cooling systems for AI data centres, and how much of the theme is already priced in.

summary.one_line: Prices were flat this week: the quote pages have not updated since 13 Nov, after a month in which all five core names fell. The new information is Aeroflex's concall. It raised its FY27 skid-revenue target to Rs 150-200 cr, but in India its liquid-cooling skids still go to one customer under an exclusive arrangement. Mordor now forecasts India's data-centre cooling market growing about 25% a year to 2032, with liquid cooling the fastest-growing segment.
key_points: IndexBox forecasts an 18.5% CAGR for direct-to-chip cooling over 2026-2035, though the same page also gives a 12.0% baseline (S1). It forecasts 15.2% for immersion-cooling fluids (S2). It puts air cooling's limit at 30 kW per rack, while AI racks exceed 100 kW (S1).

New: Mordor Intelligence values India's data-centre cooling market at USD 2.99 bn in 2026. It forecasts USD 11.38 bn by 2032, a 24.86% CAGR over 2027-2032. It expects liquid cooling to grow fastest, at a 26.7% CAGR, while air cooling still holds 65.85% of the market in 2026 (S4).

JLL puts India's data-centre capacity at 1.6 GW in mid-2026 and expects 6 GW by 2029 (S3). India's first direct-to-chip hyperscale deployment is Vertiv's 30 MW system at CapitaLand's Airoli site, and Vertiv makes its own secondary-fluid-network (SFN) skids for it in India (S23).

New: On its Q2 FY27 call, Aeroflex raised its FY27 skid-revenue target to Rs 150-200 cr from about Rs 125 cr. It said data centres are now its largest vertical, and it guided to FY30 revenue of close to Rs 1,500 cr (S22). H1 FY27 skid revenue was Rs 82.42 cr: Rs 32.39 cr in Q1 and Rs 50.03 cr in Q2 (our sum, from S6).

New: Aeroflex said it supplies liquid cooling in India exclusively to one customer, a 'large US multinational'. The exclusivity does not apply outside India, and talks with that customer about overseas supply are at an advanced stage. Talks with other international players are at an earlier stage (S12). Capacity is 12,000 skids a year, with 15,000 due by December 2026 and 30,000 by March 2028. Management expects 40-50% utilisation this year (S12).

KRN doubled Q2 FY27 revenue to Rs 319.14 cr, but its EBITDA margin fell to 15.27% from 19.90%, and it gave no data-centre share (S20). In FY26, data centres were about 16% of revenue (S9). The stock is down 25.8% over one month (S16).

The fluids leg is still undisclosed. Savita's Q2 FY27 revenue rose 58.9% to Rs 1,709.39 cr, and the results coverage does not mention data-centre coolants (S19, S8). Apar discloses no Poweroil DC 10 revenue (S11). Navin Fluorine targets completion of its Chemours immersion-fluid project by end-Q3 FY27, with deliveries in Q4 FY27 (S25).

for_investors.title: Who benefits
points: Aeroflex: it raised its FY27 skid-revenue target to Rs 150-200 cr (S22). Skid volumes rose from 1,040 units in Q1 to 1,475 in Q2 (S6). Its exclusivity covers only India, so it is free to sell overseas, and talks with its existing customer about overseas supply are at an advanced stage (S12).
KRN: revenue doubled in Q2, and management says new data-centre customers have started working with it (S20). It has passed Vertiv's quality audit (S9).
Navin Fluorine: purchase orders are in place for Q4 FY27 delivery from the Chemours project (S25).

Savita and Apar have data-centre fluids on the market, QuantiCool PG 25 and Poweroil DC 10. That is an option the market is not yet paying for, since neither discloses revenue from them (S8, S11). Mordor expects liquid to be India's fastest-growing cooling segment (S4).

for_investors.title: Who is hurt / risks
points: Aeroflex sells liquid cooling in India to one customer, under an exclusive arrangement. It does not bid directly to data-centre end users, and it does not disclose its order book (S12).
Global OEMs are localising the parts Indian small caps sell. Vertiv makes its own SFN skids in India (S23) and supplies CDUs to Netweb (S14).

Aeroflex faces a Rs 41.76 cr tax demand for AY2018-19, which it is appealing (S5). Its Rs 202 cr plan is partly funded by equity and a bridge loan (S21). Some of its Q2 profit growth came from a depreciation-method change worth Rs 8.41 cr (S6).
KRN's margin is falling as it scales, to a 15.27% EBITDA margin from 19.90% (S20), and its FY26 operating cash flow was -Rs 113.80 cr (S9).
Air cooling still holds about two-thirds of India's data-centre cooling market (65.85% in 2026, S4), so the liquid share will take years to build.

for_investors.title: What to watch
points: Whether Aeroflex reaches 15,000 skid units a year by December 2026, and its H2 skid revenue. Implied H2 revenue is Rs 68-118 cr: the Rs 150-200 cr target less H1's Rs 82.42 cr (our calculation, from S6 and S22).
A first overseas skid order for Aeroflex, or a second liquid-cooling customer (S12).
Completion of Navin's Chemours project by end-Q3 FY27 and first deliveries in Q4 FY27 (S25).

Whether KRN discloses a data-centre revenue share for FY27 (FY26: about 16%) (S9, S20). Whether Savita or Apar first disclose data-centre fluid revenue (S8, S11, S19). The launch of Blue Star's CDU (S24).

sections.title: Theme explainer: why AI is forcing liquid cooling

blocks.text: Liquid cooling removes heat with a fluid instead of air. In direct-to-chip (DTC) systems, a coolant runs through cold plates on the processors. The coolant is typically a glycol/water mix, such as Savita's QuantiCool PG 25 (S8). Coolant distribution units (CDUs), manifolds, SFN skids and hoses circulate it, and heat exchangers pass the heat to facility water (S23). In immersion cooling, servers sit in a dielectric (non-conductive) fluid. Examples are Apar's single-phase Poweroil DC 10 (S11) and the Chemours two-phase fluid that Navin Fluorine is preparing to make (S25). IndexBox says air cooling reaches its physical limit above 30 kW per rack and is no longer viable for hyperscalers above 50 kW, while AI/ML racks exceed 100 kW (S1).

blocks.caption: Liquid-cooling forecasts (the forecasters' figures, not ours)

blocks.text: IndexBox puts data centres at 45% of immersion-fluid demand in 2026. The rest is EV batteries (20%), HPC (15%), power transformers (10%) and crypto mining (10%) (S2). Indian fluid makers can therefore fill capacity from non-data-centre demand while data-centre orders build. We did not find a MarketsandMarkets figure we could open, so none is shown.

sections.title: India build-out, capex and local content

subsections.title: India data-centre pipeline and the liquid share

blocks.text: JLL's mid-year report estimates India's capacity at 1.6 GW in mid-2026 and forecasts 6 GW by 2029. H1 2026 absorption was 101 MW, 82% of it pre-committed hyperscale capacity. JLL lists liquid, direct-to-chip and immersion cooling among the practices being adopted (S3). Vertiv describes CLDC Mumbai 01 in Airoli as India's first direct-to-chip, high-density liquid-cooling deployment. It supports 30 MW of AI workloads for a hyperscale customer (S23). Mordor gives the closest available answer on air versus liquid: air-based cooling holds 65.85% of India's data-centre cooling market in 2026, and liquid-based cooling is the fastest-growing segment at a 26.7% CAGR over 2027-2032 (S4).

blocks.text: Mordor does not state a liquid share directly, and we have not derived one, because the page may include segments other than air and liquid. The only confirmed DTC hyperscale deployment in India so far is the 30 MW at Airoli (S23), small against JLL's 1.6 GW base (S3).

items: Made in India by listed companies: Aeroflex skids and hoses (S6, S12), KRN coils (S9, S20), and Savita and Apar fluids (S8, S11). Navin's two-phase fluid has not yet been delivered (S25).

Global OEMs are localising the same items. Vertiv makes SFN skids in India (S23) and supplies CDUs and chillers for Netweb's systems (S14). Aeroflex does not name its sole Indian liquid-cooling customer, describing it only as a 'large US multinational' (S12).
We found no Indian listed company with commercial CDU or cold-plate output. Blue Star's CDU and KRN's liquid-cooling products are still in development (S20, S24).

blocks.text: Aeroflex's Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs 207.36 cr, against Rs 110.87 cr a year earlier. EBITDA rose 94.49% to Rs 50.34 cr and PAT rose 156.85% to Rs 36.56 cr, helped by an Rs 8.41 cr cut in depreciation from a method change. Skids brought in Rs 50.03 cr from 1,475 units, against Rs 32.39 cr from 1,040 units in Q1 (S6). On the call, management said data centres are now the largest vertical. It raised the FY27 skid-revenue target to Rs 150-200 cr from about Rs 125 cr and guided to FY30 revenue of close to Rs 1,500 cr at margins of about 25%. An analyst on the call put average realisation at Rs 3.39 lakh per skid (S22). Management also said the company works exclusively with one customer for liquid cooling in India, does not bid directly to data-centre end users, and does not disclose its order book (S12). KRN's Q2 FY27 revenue rose 109.86% to Rs 319.14 cr and PAT rose 100.3% to Rs 36.11 cr, but the EBITDA margin fell to 15.27% from 19.90%. Management named data-centre cooling and liquid-cooling product development as growth areas but gave no data-centre revenue share (S20).

subsections.title: Fluids leg: products ready, revenue undisclosed

blocks.text: Savita's Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 58.88% to Rs 1,709.39 cr, and PAT rose to Rs 211.86 cr from Rs 40.59 cr, but PAT was down 26.5% from Q1's Rs 288.06 cr. The coverage gives no data-centre, coolant or ester detail (S19). Savita's data-centre page lists QuantiCool PG 25 for direct liquid cooling and names no customers or revenue (S8). Its Phase 2 synthetic-ester plant at Mahad was commissioned on 28 Feb 2026, and the filing says esters suit data-centre cooling fluids (S10). Apar markets Poweroil DC 10 for single-phase immersion (S11) but does not disclose revenue from it. Castrol India says data-centre cooling is not yet material (S13). Navin Fluorine's Q2 FY27 revenue rose 57% to Rs 1,190.7 cr. Management targets completion of the Chemours project by end-Q3 FY27, with purchase orders in place for delivery in Q4 FY27 (S25).

Coverage by size: the two small caps, Aeroflex and KRN, are still the only names that report quantified data-centre cooling revenue (S6, S9). Savita, also a small cap, has products but no disclosed revenue (S8, S19). The mid caps (Castrol, Blue Star, Netweb) and the large caps (Apar, Navin Fluorine) have products or adjacencies but no disclosed data-centre cooling revenue (S11, S13, S14, S24, S25). The Indian CDU makers we found, Refroid and KuhlTherm, are unlisted, and Schneider's Motivair plant in Bengaluru belongs to a foreign parent, so all three are excluded.

items: The hoses and heat-exchanger legs have been re-rated. Aeroflex is up 174.5% over one year despite falling 9.0% in the past month (S7). KRN is up 27.2% over a year but down 25.8% over one month (S16).

The fluids leg's returns are not driven by data centres. Savita is up 58.7% over six months on its base-oil profit surge, but down 12.5% over one month (S15, S19). Apar is down 18.5% over one month (S17). Neither discloses data-centre fluid revenue (S8, S11).

Broker coverage is still thin. On the calls, sell-side analysts are asking about skid realisation and capacity (S22). Otherwise coverage comes mainly from retail and fintech media, such as DSIJ and Multibagg on Aeroflex (S6, S12) and Trade Brains' supplier roundup (S24).

blocks.text: The Anand Rathi pages are internally inconsistent. Each page gives two P/E figures (Aeroflex: 75.0 in the fundamentals section, 58.72 in the FAQ), and the narrative returns differ from the tables. We use the table values and treat them as indicative (S7, S15, S16, S17, S18).

items: Single-customer dependence: Aeroflex works exclusively with one customer for liquid cooling in India, does not bid to data-centre end users, and discloses neither its client count nor its order book (S12).

OEM localisation: Vertiv makes SFN skids at its own India facility for the country's first DTC deployment (S23). Trade Brains flags competition from Vertiv, Schneider and Johnson Controls for hyperscale work (S24).

Utilisation and funding: Aeroflex expects only 40-50% skid utilisation this year while it doubles capacity (S12). The Rs 202 cr plan uses equity and a bridge loan, so shareholders could be diluted (S21).
Tax dispute: Aeroflex faces a Rs 41.76 cr income-tax demand for AY2018-19 and is appealing (S5).
Margins and working capital: KRN's Q2 EBITDA margin fell 4.63 points to 15.27% (S20), and its FY26 operating cash flow was -Rs 113.80 cr (S9).
Adoption pace: air still holds 65.85% of India's data-centre cooling market (S4), and Blue Star's liquid-cooling products remain in development (S24).

companies.name: Aeroflex Industries Ltd
companies.role: Makes stainless-steel flexible hoses and liquid-cooling SFN skid assemblies. In India it supplies liquid cooling exclusively to one large US multinational customer (S6, S12).
companies.impact: Skids brought in Rs 50.03 cr in Q2 FY27 (S6), and the FY27 skid target was raised to Rs 150-200 cr (S22). Capacity is rising to 15,000 units by December 2026 and 30,000 by March 2028 (S12). It depends on one customer and faces a Rs 41.76 cr tax demand (S5, S12). The stock is up 174.5% over one year (S7).

companies.name: KRN Heat Exchanger and Refrigeration Ltd
companies.role: Makes fin-and-tube heat-exchanger coils for HVAC&R, including data-centre cooling. It has passed Vertiv's quality audit and is developing liquid-cooling products (S9, S20).
companies.impact: Q2 FY27 revenue doubled to Rs 319.14 cr, but the EBITDA margin fell to 15.27% and no data-centre share was disclosed (S20). Data centres were about 16% of FY26 revenue (S9). The stock is down 25.8% over one month (S16).

companies.name: Blue Star Ltd
companies.role: Supplies data-centre cooling, and is developing a data-centre chiller and a liquid-cooling CDU (S24).
companies.impact: It reports no liquid-cooling revenue, and its CDU models are about 12 months away from October 2026 (S24). The stock is down 10.9% over one year (S18).

companies.name: Savita Oil Technologies Ltd
companies.role: Sells QuantiCool PG 25 coolant for direct liquid cooling, and commissioned Phase 2 of its Mahad synthetic-ester plant on 28 Feb 2026 (S8, S10).
companies.impact: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 58.9% to Rs 1,709.39 cr with no data-centre detail disclosed (S19), so data-centre fluids remain an undisclosed option. The stock is down 12.5% over one month (S15).

companies.name: Apar Industries Ltd
companies.role: Markets Poweroil DC 10, a single-phase immersion dielectric fluid, alongside data-centre cables (S11).
companies.impact: It discloses no data-centre fluid revenue. The stock is down 18.5% over one month and up 65.6% over one year (S11, S17).

companies.name: Navin Fluorine International Ltd
companies.role: Is building capacity to make Chemours' two-phase immersion-cooling fluid (S25).
companies.impact: Completion is targeted for end-Q3 FY27, with purchase orders for Q4 FY27 delivery, so there is no revenue yet (S25).

companies.name: Castrol India Ltd
companies.role: Has immersion and direct-to-chip coolants ready for India and in tests with OEMs (S13).
companies.impact: Management calls data-centre cooling not yet material, so there is no near-term earnings effect (S13).

companies.name: Netweb Technologies India Ltd
companies.role: Indian server OEM that builds direct-to-chip liquid-cooled GPU systems with Vertiv's CDUs and chillers (S14).
companies.impact: A downstream adjacency: it pulls liquid-cooling content through its systems rather than making fluids or hardware (S14).

method:
W47 refresh of the W46 edition, researched on 2026-11-16 with web search and page fetches.

New this week:
- Aeroflex Q2 FY27 concall, from two Multibagg write-ups dated 2 Nov (S12, S22): the FY27 skid-revenue target raised to Rs 150-200 cr; an exclusive single-customer arrangement for liquid cooling in India; no exclusivity overseas; 40-50% utilisation expected this year; FY30 revenue guided to close to Rs 1,500 cr. The concall describes the customer as a 'large US multinational'. Earlier editions called it 'US-listed' (from an ICICI Securities note); we have dropped that wording.
- Mordor Intelligence's India data-centre cooling page, updated 23 Oct 2026 (S4), which addresses the brief's air-versus-liquid question.

Re-verified: all five Anand Rathi quote pages were re-opened on 16 Nov. Their tables are still dated 13 Nov and the values are unchanged. Their P/E figures differ from the dashboard's screener.in feed (e.g. KRN 101.4 vs 58.3), so readers should rely on the dashboard for valuation.

Read but not cited: Wissen Research (PR Newswire, 11 Nov 2026), which forecasts a USD 42 bn global data-centre cooling market by 2031 at a 16.5% CAGR, has no liquid-specific figure, and is a lesser-known research house. Apar's Q2 FY27 call summary (InvestyWise, 4 Nov) shows oil-segment revenue up 35.6% on base-oil prices, with no mention of Poweroil or data-centre fluids. It was left out to stay within the source limit. An Informist Blue Star concall note from Nov 2025, which is stale. KRN's Outlook Business H1 press release, which duplicates S20.

Dropped to stay within 25 sources:
- The ICICI Securities Aeroflex note.
- InvestyWise on Blue Star's Q2, so Blue Star's Q2 revenue and project-delay points are removed; the dashboard carries the financials.
- DSIJ on Navin's original Rs 120 cr capex and Q1 FY27 target, so the 'timeline slipped' point is removed.

Screened but excluded: Refroid and KuhlTherm (unlisted CDU makers) and Schneider/Motivair (foreign parent). Voltas, Gulf Oil and BPCL were excluded in earlier editions because none has confirmed liquid-cooling products. No new qualifying listed name was found this week.

Carried over without re-opening: S1-S3, S5, S6, S8-S11, S13, S14, S19-S21, S23-S25.

Our calculations: Aeroflex's H1 skid revenue, its skid share of Q2 revenue, and the implied H2 skid revenue (from S6 and S22).

No ratings or price targets.
